answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards as a condition for identity, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits. Like a dawn breaking over a digital frontier, the verifier probes random segments, and any failed proof of replication triggers a non-refundable slash of deposited funds. An honest node incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to complete their voyage. Every shard delta acts as a unique digital pigment, ensuring no collusion. The audit remains binding for 30 days.
